content.text: A robust mutual insurance regime exists at Section 11.6. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 11.6 Insurance. Each Party shall obtain and carry in full force and effect the minimum insurance requirements set forth herein. Such insurance (a) shall be primary insurance with respect to each Party's own participation under this Agreement, (b) shall be issued by a recognized insurer rated by A.M. Best "A-VII" (or its equivalent) or better, or an insurer pre- approved in writing by the other Party, and (c) shall list the other Party as an additional insured under the General Liability Policy.
input.rationale: Section 11.6 contains a usable insurance covenant, so the rule is not missing. It obliges each Party (including Harpoon) to carry, throughout the Agreement, workers' compensation at statutory limits (11.6.1(a)), employer's liability (11.6.1(b)) and general liability including Clinical Trial Insurance on a per-occurrence and aggregate basis (11.6.1(c)), from A.M. Best "A-VII" or better carriers, with AbbVie named as additional insured, certificates of insurance on request, and post-termination tail cover where only claims-made policies are available (11.6.2). That covers the preferred position's CGL, workers' compensation and certificates-on-request elements, and Section 11.6.3 additionally preserves AbbVie's right to self-insure — a term that benefits us and should not be disturbed. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: (i) the dollar limits in 11.6.1(b)-(c) and the tail period in 11.6.2 are redacted as [***], so quantum cannot be verified from the face of the document and should be confirmed against the disclosure schedules; and (ii) there is no separate professional liability (E&O) or cyber/privacy line. The cyber gap is not material in this deal type — this is a development and option collaboration for licensed compounds, not a services or hosting engagement in which Harpoon processes AbbVie personal data or works on our premises, so the walk-away trigger (no insurance for a data-processing or on-site vendor) is not engaged, and the clinical-trial-specific general liability cover is the risk-appropriate substitute. Treating this as sitting at or above the fallback, the clause is compliant and we should not redline it.
